prompt: In a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle the hypotenuse is $12$. How long is the side opposite the $30^\circ$ angle?
hint: The sides are in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$, and the hypotenuse matches the $2$.

hints.text: The sides are in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$, and the hypotenuse matches the $2$.
If $2$ corresponds to $12$, the scale factor is $6$. Multiply the $1$ by that factor.
The short side is $1 \times 6 = 6$ — exactly half the hypotenuse.

explanation: A $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle always has sides in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$ (short leg : long leg : hypotenuse).
The hypotenuse $12$ corresponds to the $2$, so every side is scaled by $\frac{12}{2} = 6$.

alternativeExplanations.title: The half-the-hypotenuse rule
steps: The side opposite the $30^\circ$ angle is always exactly half the hypotenuse.
Half of 12 is 6. The other leg, $6\sqrt{3} \approx 10.4$, is the one opposite $60^\circ$ — the bigger angle always faces the bigger side.
